newsitem.title: USA: Farm secretary declares disaster areas in Alaska.
newsitem.headline: Farm secretary declares disaster areas in Alaska.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman has declared regions of Alaska disaster areas because of an extended drought, state officials said Friday.

In a letter sent to Gov. Tony Knowles this week, Glickman named the Fairbanks-North Star Borough, southeast Fairbanks-Delta area, Matanuska-Susitna Borough and Kenai Peninsula as areas where farmers will be eligible to recover disaster aid.

"I requested the disaster designation in July and instructed my administration to work closely with federal officials to ensure a disaster declaration for the farmers in Alaska," Knowles said in a news release.

The areas were affected by a snow drought last year that was compounded with especially cold temperatures. Without an insulating layer of snow, the ground froze to deep levels, and subsequently dried out, officials said.

Only a few farm operations will be eligible for the aid, said Alaska Division of Agriculture Director Jay Kerttula. They must have both livestock and produce, and must have sustained a production loss of 30 percent or more during the past year, Kerttula said.
Alaska farmers with irrigation systems fared well despite the drought, and were able to produce bumper crops in the past year, he said.

Dry conditions in the Matanuska-Susitana Borough were blamed for the spread of a devastating June wildfire that destoyed over 300 structures. It damaged more property than any other wildfire in Alaska history.
